positions.as_written: No index reports the transverse offset and the height together, so both must be stated.
Report the tubercle to groove distance and a named height ratio together, because they describe different problems.
Record the knee position at imaging, since the transverse index depends on it.
Expect medialisation to reduce the lateral vector and distalisation to advance engagement, and keep the two decisions separate.
Avoid treating a single borderline index as an indication, because both thresholds are soft.
- Height ratios disagree systematically, so the ratio must be named.
Decide direction and magnitude separately, since medialisation and distalisation correct different mechanisms.
Limit medialisation, because medial facet overload is the characteristic complication.
State that the pressure redistribution is inferred rather than measured after surgery.

Take the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations into the decision, because a precise correction of one term does not by itself make the operation right for this patient.
